source_refs.note: Exercise 11.2, Question 2: book page 292 (Q1-Q2). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the first-order derivative of the following vector-valued function with respect to \(t\) at the specified value of \(t\): \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \left(\frac{t^2 + 1}{\sin t}\right)\hat{i} + \left(\sqrt{t}\,e^t\right)\hat{j}\) at \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Is qism ke sawal mein pehle derivative nikalte hain, phir \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) rakhte hain.
\(\hat{i}\) mein fraction hai, is liye quotient rule; \(\hat{j}\) mein do functions ka product, is liye product rule. Kitab mein root sirf \(t\) par hai: \(\sqrt{t}\,e^t\).
Faida: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) aur \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) se kaam bohat chhota ho jata hai.
Plan: general \(\mathbf{r}'(t)\), phir \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) par value.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \frac{t^2 + 1}{\sin t}\,\hat{i} + \sqrt{t}\,e^t\,\hat{j}\), \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}'\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
Tareeqa: 11.4 ki definition ke mutabiq \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = f_1'(t)\,\hat{i} + f_2'(t)\,\hat{j} + f_3'(t)\,\hat{k}\): har component ko aam function ki tarah differentiate karein; unit vectors constant hain, apni jagah rehte hain. Phir \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) rakhein.

\(\hat{i}\)-component: quotient rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{t^2 + 1}{\sin t}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{2t\sin t - (t^2 + 1)\cos t}{\sin^2 t}\]
Kyun: \(\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)' = \frac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}\), jahan \(u = t^2 + 1\) (oopar wala), \(v = \sin t\) (neeche wala). Yaad karne ka tareeqa: "neeche wala \(\times\) oopar ka derivative, minus oopar wala \(\times\) neeche ka derivative, sab neeche ke square par".
Dhyan dein: numerator mein tarteeb (order) ulti ho jaye to sign ulta aa jata hai.

\(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par value
\[\dfrac{2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} \cdot 1 - \left(\frac{\pi^2}{4} + 1\right) \cdot 0}{1^2} = \pi\]
Kyun: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\), \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\), is liye doosra poora term zero ho gaya aur denominator 1 raha. Value rakhne se pehle aise zero pehchan lena waqt bachata hai.

\(\hat{j}\)-component: product rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\sqrt{t}\,e^t\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,e^t + \sqrt{t}\,e^t\]
\[= \dfrac{e^t(1 + 2t)}{2\sqrt{t}}\]
Kyun: \(u = \sqrt{t}\), \(u' = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\); \(v = e^t\), \(v' = e^t\) (\(e^t\) ka derivative khud \(e^t\)). Denominator \(2\sqrt{t}\) common kiya: \(\sqrt{t} = \frac{2t}{2\sqrt{t}}\).

\(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par value
\[\dfrac{e^{\pi/2}(1 + \pi)}{2\sqrt{\pi/2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{(1 + \pi)\,e^{\pi/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\]
\[\approx \dfrac{4.1416 \times 4.8105}{2.5066} \approx 7.95\]
Kyun: \(2\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}} = \sqrt{4 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2}} = \sqrt{2\pi}\): bahar ka 2 andar jate hue 4 ban jata hai.

Dono ko jorein
\[\mathbf{r}'\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pi\,\hat{i}\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{(1 + \pi)\,e^{\pi/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,\hat{j}\]
Tasdeeq: sympy dono components ke liye \(\pi \approx 3.1416\) aur \(7.9481\) deta hai \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: exact jawab hi asal jawab hai; decimal sirf andaza dikhane ke liye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.2 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (balke poore Unit 11 ke nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the first-order derivative of the following vector-valued function with respect to \(t\) at the specified value of \(t\): \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \left(t\sqrt{t + 2}\right)\hat{i} + \ln\left(t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}\right)\hat{j}\) at \(t = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Pehle derivative, phir \(t = 0\).
\(\hat{i}\) mein product rule (saath square root bhi), aur \(\hat{j}\) mein log par chain rule, jo aakhir mein bohat khoobsurti se chhota ho jata hai.
Rule: \(\frac{d}{dt}\ln u = \frac{u'}{u}\) aur \(\frac{d}{dt}\sqrt{u} = \frac{u'}{2\sqrt{u}}\).
Plan: general derivatives, simplify, phir value.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = t\sqrt{t + 2}\,\hat{i} + \ln\left(t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}\right)\hat{j}\), \(t = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}'(0)\).
Tareeqa: 11.4 ki definition ke mutabiq \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = f_1'(t)\,\hat{i} + f_2'(t)\,\hat{j} + f_3'(t)\,\hat{k}\): har component ko aam function ki tarah differentiate karein; unit vectors constant hain, apni jagah rehte hain. Phir \(t = 0\) rakhein.

\(\hat{i}\)-component: product rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(t\sqrt{t + 2}\right)\]
\[= \sqrt{t + 2} + \dfrac{t}{2\sqrt{t + 2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2(t + 2) + t}{2\sqrt{t + 2}} = \dfrac{3t + 4}{2\sqrt{t + 2}}\]
Kyun: \(u = t\) (derivative 1), \(v = \sqrt{t + 2}\) (derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t + 2}}\)). Phir common denominator \(2\sqrt{t + 2}\) bana kar ek fraction mein likha.

\(t = 0\) par
\[\dfrac{4}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\) ko \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}\) se multiply karein to \(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2} = \sqrt{2}\) (rationalize karna).

\(\hat{j}\)-component: chain rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\ln\left(t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}}\left(1 + \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{t^2 + 1}}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{t^2 + 1} + t}{\sqrt{t^2 + 1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{t^2 + 1}}\]
Kyun: \(u = t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}\). Is ka derivative \(1 + \frac{2t}{2\sqrt{t^2 + 1}} = 1 + \frac{t}{\sqrt{t^2 + 1}}\). Bracket ko ek fraction banaya to numerator mein wahi \(t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}\) aa gaya jo denominator mein tha, aur dono cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: bracket ko jaldi se \(t = 0\) rakh kar mat chhoriye; simplify karne se kaam aasan hota hai.

\(t = 0\) par
\[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0 + 1}} = 1\]
\[\mathbf{r}'(0) = \sqrt{2}\,\hat{i} + \hat{j}\]
Tasdeeq: \(\ln\left(t + \sqrt{t^2 + 1}\right) = \sinh^{-1} t\) (Unit 1), aur \(\frac{d}{dt}\sinh^{-1} t = \frac{1}{\sqrt{t^2 + 1}}\) \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: do alag raaston se ek hi jawab aana is baat ki pakki daleel hai ke kaam sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find the first-order derivative of the following vector-valued function with respect to \(t\) at the specified value of \(t\): \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \arctan(t)\,\hat{i} + \frac{\sin(t^2)}{t}\,\hat{j} + \sqrt[3]{1 + t}\,\hat{k}\) at \(t = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Har component ko differentiate kar ke \(t = 0\) par value nikalni hai.
Lekin khabardar: \(\hat{j}\) wala component \(\frac{\sin(t^2)}{t}\) \(t = 0\) par \(\frac{0}{0}\) ban jata hai, yani wahan defined hi nahin (neeche correction dekhein).
Rule: aisi jagah "hole" (khali jagah) ko limit se bharte hain, phir derivative ki definition lagate hain.
Plan: \(\hat{i}\) aur \(\hat{k}\) aam tareeqe se; \(\hat{j}\) ke liye limit.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \arctan t\,\hat{i} + \frac{\sin(t^2)}{t}\,\hat{j} + \sqrt[3]{1 + t}\,\hat{k}\), \(t = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}'(0)\).
Tareeqa: 11.4 ki definition ke mutabiq \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = f_1'(t)\,\hat{i} + f_2'(t)\,\hat{j} + f_3'(t)\,\hat{k}\): har component ko aam function ki tarah differentiate karein; unit vectors constant hain, apni jagah rehte hain. \(\hat{j}\) wala component \(0\) par defined nahin, us ke liye limits.

\(\hat{i}\)-component
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\arctan t = \dfrac{1}{1 + t^2}\]
\[t = 0 \text{ par: } \dfrac{1}{1 + 0} = 1\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1} t\) (arctan) ka standard derivative. \(\arctan\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) ek hi cheez ke do naam hain.

\(\hat{k}\)-component
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(1 + t)^{1/3} = \dfrac{1}{3}(1 + t)^{-2/3}\]
\[t = 0 \text{ par: } \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: cube root ko power \(\frac{1}{3}\) likha; power rule lagaya, aur andar \(1 + t\) ka derivative 1 hai. \(t = 0\) par \((1)^{-2/3} = 1\).

\(\hat{j}\)-component, jab \(t \ne 0\)
Maan lein \(g(t) = \frac{\sin(t^2)}{t}\).
\[g'(t) = \dfrac{t \cdot 2t\cos(t^2) - \sin(t^2)}{t^2}\]
\[= 2\cos(t^2) - \dfrac{\sin(t^2)}{t^2}\]
Kyun: quotient rule, aur \(\sin(t^2)\) par chain rule: \(\frac{d}{dt}\sin(t^2) = \cos(t^2) \cdot 2t\). Lekin is formula mein bhi \(t = 0\) rakhein to phir \(\frac{0}{0}\) aata hai, is liye limit chahiye.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{\sin(t^2)}{t^2}\) mein \(t = 0\) rakh kar seedha 0 ya 1 likh dena ghalat hai.

\(t = 0\) par hole bharein
\[\lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sin(t^2)}{t}\]
\[= \lim_{t \to 0}\left(t \cdot \dfrac{\sin(t^2)}{t^2}\right)\]
\[= 0 \times 1 = 0\]
Is liye hum \(g(0) = 0\) maan lete hain; ab \(g\) zero par continuous hai.
Kyun: standard limit \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta = t^2\). Upar neeche \(t\) se multiply kar ke yeh shakal banayi.

Definition se zero par derivative
\[g'(0) = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0}\dfrac{g(\Delta t) - g(0)}{\Delta t}\]
\[= \lim_{\Delta t \to 0}\dfrac{\sin((\Delta t)^2)}{(\Delta t)^2} = 1\]
Kyun: \(\frac{g(\Delta t) - 0}{\Delta t} = \frac{\sin((\Delta t)^2)}{\Delta t \cdot \Delta t}\), aur wahi standard limit 1 deti hai. Jab formula kaam na kare to hamesha definition par wapas jayein.

Sab ko jorein
\[\mathbf{r}'(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \tfrac{1}{3}\,\hat{k}\]
Tasdeeq: \(\lim_{t \to 0} g'(t) = 2\cos 0 - 1 = 1\) bhi aata hai, is liye \(\lim_{t \to 0}\mathbf{r}'(t) = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\) \(\checkmark\) (sympy bhi yahi kehta hai).
Kyun: do alag tareeqon se ek hi nateeja aaya.
blocks.final_answer: Kitab ke mutabiq \(\mathbf{r}(0)\) defined nahin, is liye \(\mathbf{r}'(0)\) mojood nahin. \(\hat{j}\) wale component ko \(t = 0\) par us ki limit wali value 0 de dein to: \(\mathbf{r}'(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \frac{1}{3}\,\hat{k}\) (jo \(\lim_{t \to 0}\mathbf{r}'(t)\) ke barabar bhi hai).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Part (iii) \(t = 0\) par derivative maangta hai, lekin wahan \(\hat{j}\) wala component \(\frac{\sin(t^2)}{t}\) \(\frac{0}{0}\) ban jata hai: \(\mathbf{r}(0)\) mojood hi nahin, aur kisi point par derivative tabhi ho sakta hai jab function wahan defined ho. Is liye kitab ke alfaz ke mutabiq \(\mathbf{r}'(0)\) mojood nahin. Yeh khali jagah sirf ek "hole" hai jo bhar sakta hai, kyunke \(\lim_{t \to 0}\frac{\sin(t^2)}{t} = 0\). \(\hat{j}\) wale component ko \(t = 0\) par value 0 de dein to \(\mathbf{r}'(0) = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\) aata hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Find the first-order derivative of the following vector-valued function with respect to \(t\) at the specified value of \(t\): \(\mathbf{r}(t) = te^{-t}\,\hat{i} + \cos(3t)\,\hat{j} + \ln(1 + t^2)\,\hat{k}\) at \(t = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Pehle derivative, phir \(t = 0\).
\(\hat{i}\) mein product rule; \(\hat{j}\) aur \(\hat{k}\) mein chain rule.
Rule: andar koi function ho (jaise \(3t\), \(-t\), \(1 + t^2\)) to us ka derivative bhi multiply hota hai.
Plan: general derivatives, phir value rakhna.
Yaad rahe: zero wale components bhi likh kar dikhayein, phir saada shakal \(\hat{i}\) likhein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = te^{-t}\,\hat{i} + \cos(3t)\,\hat{j} + \ln(1 + t^2)\,\hat{k}\), \(t = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}'(0)\).
Tareeqa: 11.4 ki definition ke mutabiq \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = f_1'(t)\,\hat{i} + f_2'(t)\,\hat{j} + f_3'(t)\,\hat{k}\): har component ko aam function ki tarah differentiate karein; unit vectors constant hain, apni jagah rehte hain. Phir \(t = 0\) rakhein.

\(\hat{i}\)-component: product rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(te^{-t}\right) = e^{-t} + t(-e^{-t})\]
\[= (1 - t)e^{-t}\]
\[t = 0 \text{ par: } (1)(1) = 1\]
Kyun: \(u = t\), \(v = e^{-t}\). \(e^{-t}\) ka derivative \(-e^{-t}\) hai (chain rule: andar \(-t\) ka derivative \(-1\)). Phir \(e^{-t}\) common nikala.
Dhyan dein: \(e^{-t}\) ka derivative \(e^{-t}\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; minus zaroor lagayein.

\(\hat{j}\)-component: chain rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\cos(3t) = -3\sin(3t)\]
\[t = 0 \text{ par: } -3\sin 0 = 0\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dt}\cos u = -\sin u \cdot u'\), jahan \(u = 3t\), \(u' = 3\). \(\sin 0 = 0\), is liye yeh component zero.

\(\hat{k}\)-component: chain rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\ln(1 + t^2) = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^2}\]
\[t = 0 \text{ par: } 0\]
Kyun: bilkul Question 1(ii) ki tarah; numerator \(2t\) zero par zero ho jata hai.

Sab ko jorein
\[\mathbf{r}'(t) = (1 - t)e^{-t}\,\hat{i} - 3\sin(3t)\,\hat{j}\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^2}\,\hat{k}\]
\[\mathbf{r}'(0) = \hat{i} + 0\,\hat{j} + 0\,\hat{k} = \hat{i}\]
Tasdeeq: sympy bhi \(\langle 1, 0, 0\rangle\) deta hai \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: \(t = 0\) par \(\mathbf{r}\) sirf \(\hat{i}\) (\(x\)) ki simt mein badal raha hai; \(y\) aur \(z\) us lamhe ruke hue hain.
